title: onboarding-heatmap-mentor-ladder-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for a cross-role onboarding approach that combines: (1) a lightweight hiring-plan snapshot, (2) a skills heatmap to triage early ramping, and (3) a Mentor Ladder with clear expectations for 0–90d.

Target audience: hiring managers, people ops, hiring panel members, new hire mentors.

Status: draft — we expect iteration after 1 pilot cohort (Oct 2025). Notes-to-self throughout (TODO).

---

1) Hiring plan snapshot (quick view)
- Q4 2025 headcount ask (summarized):
  - Backend Engineer (platform) — 2 FTE 
  - Applied ML Engineer — 1 FTE (serving-runtime focus)
  - Product Designer — 1 FTE (console UX)
  - Solutions Engineer — 1 FTE (pilot customers)
  - People Ops Coordinator — 0.5 FTE (temp contractor -> perm)
- Priority order: platform eng > applied ML > solutions > design > people ops coord
- Ramp target: first contribution within 30d for infra/platform; 60–90d for product/design.
- Hiring cadence: 2-week interview sprints, rolling offers end-of-sprint.

Quick hiring notes: keep interview loops to max 4 stages, include one cross-functional pairing exercise (not whiteboard). Use standardized rubric (see section 3).

---

2) Skills heatmap (text-first, lightweight)
- Purpose: at offer-acceptance and day0, map 8 core capabilities across role cluster to prioritize 0–30d learning tasks and pairings.
- How to read: 3 = high proficiency expected at hire, 2 = working knowledge OK, 1 = ramp on job, 0 = not required.

Roles (columns): platform-eng, applied-ml, product-design, solutions-eng
Skills (rows): python, infra-k8s, GPU-inferencing, observability, sql/data, ux-prototyping, customer-requests, security-compliance
Heatmap table (comma-separated for clipboard):
python,3,3,2,2
infra-k8s,3,1,0,1
GPU-inferencing,2,3,0,1
observability,3,2,1,2
sql/data,2,3,1,2
ux-prototyping,0,0,3,1
customer-requests,1,1,1,3
security-compliance,2,2,1,2

Example usage: new applied-ml hire scores low on observability (1) at day0 -> priority pairing with SRE mentor + 2 concrete quick wins: 1) run local eval harness; 2) add perf metric to PR template.

---

3) Interview rubric (compact cheat sheet for panelists)
- Structure: 4 evidence buckets (technical craft, product sense/impact, systems thinking/reliability, collaboration/communication). Panelists assign 1-5 and add 1–2 bullet examples.
- Auto-fail signals (call these out in interview): dishonest work examples, inability to accept feedback, repeated hostility in collaboration stories.
- Example rubrics per role (short):
  - Platform Engineer:
    - technical craft (k8s, infra automation) 1-5
    - systems thinking (failure modes, SLOs) 1-5
    - shipping velocity (past examples, PRs) 1-5
    - collaboration (cross-team incident) 1-5
  - Applied ML:
    - modeling pragmatism (tradeoffs) 1-5
    - inference ops (latency/cost considerations) 1-5
    - experiment rigor (A/B design) 1-5
    - communication (explain model choice to PM) 1-5

Interview logistics reminders:
- Panelists: hire manager + 2 peers + optional partner from product/solutions.
- Timebox: 50 min total, 40 min interview + 10 min rubric writing.
- Scorecard: required fields: evidence bullets (>=1 per bucket), recommend / not recommend, concerns.

---

4) Mentor Ladder (novel — ladder levels and responsibilities)
- Goal: make mentoring explicit; avoid over-burdening ICs; distribute onboarding ownership.
- Levels:
  - Level 0: Onboarding Buddy (first 14d) — 4–6 hours/week. Focus: logistics, first PRs, connect to team rituals.
  - Level 1: Functional Mentor (day 15–60) — 2–3 hours/week. Focus: role-specific craft, code reviews, learning plan checkpoints.
  - Level 2: Career Sponsor (day 60–180) — ad-hoc monthly syncs. Focus: visibility, goals, cross-team introductions.
- Notes: the same person can serve multiple levels for small teams but try to rotate so new hire meets 3+ mentors in 90d.
- Compensation: 2 mentor credits per quarter (tracked in Lattice for recognition).

Mentor playbook (short):
- Week 0: checklist handoff (access, environment, docs)
- Week 1: pair on a production debugging ticket 
- Week 2–4: 2x code reviews + 1 small feature + 30-min learning roadmap
- Week 4–8: periodic deep dive on systems (1–2 sessions)

---

5) 0–30 day checklist (practical items)
Day0 (before first day):
- equipment shipped and tested (serials)
- accounts created (email, GitHub, Jira, GCP/AWS, internal tooling)
- first-week schedule in calendar (meet the team, product orientation)
- assign buddy + intro Slack message drafted

Day1:
- 30–60m with people ops: benefits, payroll, policies
- 90m team kickoff: mission, current priorities, codebase map
- run through dev setup doc, pair on first local run
- assign first small onboarding ticket (non-user-facing)

Day2–7:
- ship first PR (template + checklist)
- 1:1 with manager (expectations, 30/60/90 goals)
- mentor: pair on troubleshooting + observability tour
- add one learning goal to Lattice profile

Day8–30:
- take ownership of small feature or bug, drive to merge
- present short 10-min demo in team retro
- 30-day check-in: hiring manager + mentor + people ops (document progress)

Checklist pragmatics: track these as Jira onboarding tasks assigned to new-hire so progress is auditable.

---

6) Onboarding triage Kanban (columns + example tickets)
- Columns: To Do (accounts, hardware), Quick Wins (first PRs), Skill Gaps (observability, GPUs), Partnerships (product pairing), Blockers (security access), Done
- Example ticket titles:
  - "Create GCP project sandbox and grant read access"
  - "Run local inference harness + record latency"
  - "Add simple metric to service x to prove observability"
  - "Complete security training module: infra-101"

How to use: each new hire has a rapid-board template (Jira) created at offer accept. Team SRE owns the infra tickets; manager owns skill goals.

---

7) Metrics of onboarding success (what we measure)
- Time to first merged PR (target: < 14 days for platform, <21 days for other roles)
- % of 30d goals completed (target: 80%)
- Ramp NPS (pulse survey at day7, day30, day90) — target >= 8/10
- Mentorship satisfaction (mentor and mentee ratings)

---

8) Small experiments to run (pilotable this quarter)
- 2x "mentor swap" weeks: new hire pairs with mentor from another team for 1 week to broaden context. Measure: survey utility + cross-team connections.
- Scalable onboarding repo: a single container image that includes all local infra mocks + one-click run script. Track reduction in setup time.
- Micro-evals: 3 quick experiments for applied-ml hires to validate inference cost vs accuracy on sample prompts; include in ramp tasks.

---

9) Open questions / TODOs
- finalize mentor credit recognition mechanics in Lattice (TODO Aisha)
- get buy-in from SRE for 2 dedicated onboarding tickets per new hire (TODO Marco)
- define exact rubric score thresholds for hiring panel automatic recommendations (TODO: run 10 historical interviews to calibrate)
- decide whether to require design pairing for product hires (ops question)

10) Notes & links (scratch)
- Example PR template: github:repo/onboarding-scripts/pull_request_template.md
- Onboarding board template (Jira): JIRA-BOARD-ONBOARD-2025
- Slack channel for pilot kickoff: #onboard-heatmap-pilot

---

Appendix: sample quick scripts (copy/paste)
- Quick checklist for buddy to paste in Slack at day1: "Welcome @newhire! Your buddy is @buddy. Today: 9:30 meet, 11:30 pair on setup, action: open PR #onboard-setup. If blocked ping #infra."
Endnotes:
- Keep this doc intentionally short. Convert to Confluence when stable (goal: Q1 2026).
- Feedback loop: retrospective after 1st cohort -> fold changes into hiring templates and interview loops.

-- Aisha (people ops)
